name: Okinawa
title: Holidays in Okinawa
intro: Coral reefs, white beaches and whale sharks in Japan's warm southern islands. Here's what Okinawa is like with the family, when to go and how long to stay.

facts.label: Time difference
facts.value: 8 to 9 hrs ahead of the UK

facts_note: UK plugs need an adapter. Check entry rules on GOV.UK before you book.
when_to_go: April and October are warm and settled, and July is hot and sunny once the rainy season ends. The rainy season runs from about mid-May to late June. Typhoons are most likely from July to September, so travel insurance matters. Winters are mild but too cool for most swimmers.

things.name: Okinawa Churaumi Aquarium
things.blurb: A giant tank with whale sharks and manta rays, plus free dolphin shows in the park outside.

things.name: Emerald Beach
things.blurb: A sheltered, lifeguarded beach in Ocean Expo Park, next to the aquarium.

things.name: Kerama Islands
things.blurb: A fast ferry from Naha to clear water, sea turtles and some of Japan's best snorkelling.

things.name: Shurijo Castle
things.blurb: The red palace of the old Ryukyu kings. The main hall is being rebuilt after a 2019 fire.

things.name: Kokusai-dori
things.blurb: Naha's busy main street of shops, snacks and purple sweet potato everything.

things.name: Okinawa World
things.blurb: A long limestone cave walk, plus craft workshops and a traditional village.

faqs.question: Is Okinawa good for a family holiday?
faqs.answer: Yes. It's safe, clean and easy, with calm beaches, great snorkelling and the aquarium. It feels more like a tropical island than the rest of Japan.

faqs.question: How many nights do you need?
faqs.answer: A week on the main island, or ten days to add a smaller island like Zamami or Ishigaki.

faqs.question: How do you get there from the UK?
faqs.answer: There are no direct flights. Fly to Tokyo or Osaka and connect, which takes about two and a half hours. Seoul, Taipei and Hong Kong also have flights.

faqs.question: Do you need a car?
faqs.answer: It helps outside Naha, as buses are slow. Japan drives on the left, but you'll need an International Driving Permit from the Post Office as well as your licence.
